svg.title: Anhedral Init Technical Communication Map
svg.desc: A spacious connected architecture map showing exact request, response, event, storage, workflow, deployment, desktop-update, DNS, and optional self-hosted communication paths.
svg.text: One connected topology: callers, trust boundaries, protocols, state authority, and delivery control planes
Arrow points to the receiver · double-ended = request/response · dashed = deploy or configuration
Shared packages compile into the applications; DNS resolves hosts; neither is a network hop.
StoreKit / Play Billing / optional Stripe Checkout
event tells clients to refetch; payload is never entitlement truth
Bearer CRON_SECRET · cleanup and outbox flush
shared packages are code, not deployed services
Vercel service · authorization and orchestration boundary
exact CORS · rate limits · structured errors
secrets and provider credentials remain here
claim leases + duplicate guards + reviewed migrations
RevenueCat remains subscription authority; this is the app projection
Fastify performs the work and reports success/failure
API derives authoritative userId after verification
publishable key in clients · secret only on server
native/store transactions and optional web checkout
REST subscriber record resolves current entitlement
Clerk user ID becomes RevenueCat app user ID
scoped event transport, never state authority
signed-in clients receive invalidation then refetch Fastify
Mobile, extension, and desktop call the configured API URL directly.
DNS resolution is omitted from request arrows to avoid implying proxying.
Fastify authorizes metadata; clients transfer bytes using narrowly scoped signed URLs.
short TTL · exact length/type · bucket CORS
Postgres records quota, owner, status, and cleanup cursor
R2 S3 keys exist only in Fastify
bytes move directly between client and R2
A service-authenticated control Worker starts persisted execution of product-owned steps.
Bearer WORKFLOW_API_TOKEN (32+) · never a client credential
idempotent HTTP / Postgres / R2 / email / queues
64 KiB JSON · safe IDs · hashed token comparison
retry limit 5 · delay 10 s · exponential backoff
instance ID is idempotency key; business state lives elsewhere
explicit integrations added by the application
persist business outcomes outside Workflow retention
each retryable step must make its side effects idempotent
CI writes immutable artifacts first and mutable channel metadata last; devices only read.
r2.dev and direct bucket domain disabled
OS validates the signed artifact before installation
Dashed arrows change provider configuration. The lower route replaces managed Neon for that deployment.
app.<domain> resolves to the managed runtime
reverse proxy to private app port
Authority and trust rules that disambiguate the arrows above.
Clerk owns identity; Fastify verifies and derives userId.
Fastify owns authorization, validation, and orchestration.
@shared packages are compiled code with no runtime authority.
RevenueCat owns subscription truth; Postgres stores the app projection.
Postgres owns items, uploads, outbox, and processed webhook records.
Ably transports invalidation only; clients refetch authoritative state.
Private R2 stores bytes; Fastify and Workers enforce access policy.
APPLICATION_WORKFLOW persists orchestration, not business authority.
WORKFLOW_API_TOKEN, R2 S3 keys, and provider secrets remain server-side.
DNS resolves names; Vercel and Workers terminate runtime requests.
Desktop CI writes; updater Worker and Electron devices only read.
Self-hosted PostgreSQL replaces Neon only for the selected deployment.
Dashed card = opt-in or explicit product integration
